breakdown.description: The Larson–Miller parameter uses absolute temperature; 700°C must be substituted as 973 K.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification uses T = 700 (°C) instead of T = 973 K (the correct absolute temperature for 700°C). The ground truth requires substituting 973 K, but the agent repeated the original error by using 700, resulting in an incorrect calculation of log10 t_r = 13.57 and t_r ≈ 3.73 × 10^13 hours instead of the correct value derived from T = 973 K.
